faq.q: Does this page list current Langley horse properties?
faq.a: No — at reading the page carried no MLS® listing cards and no result count at all; it is an editorial page with property types, a buyer's guide and an ALR address-check tool, despite "MLS Listings" in its title

faq.q: What farm income does an equestrian property need for farm class?
faq.a: $2,500 in farm-gate sales at 0.8–4 ha, $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha above that size, and $10,000 under 0.8 ha, with applications to BC Assessment due by October 31 — not the flat "$2,500+" the live page states

faq.q: Are Langley horse properties in the City or the Township?
faq.a: The Township — the live page itself states almost all equestrian and farm properties are in the Township of Langley, a separate municipality from the City of Langley, across rural areas including Campbell Valley, Salmon River, Aldergrove, Fort Langley and the Otter District

faq.q: What should I check before buying a farm in Langley Horse Properties Equestrian Mls Listings?
faq.a: Check the ALR status, water source and licences, drainage and flood history, the buildings and any quota or production licences that do or do not transfer with the land. Poultry and egg production in BC are supply-managed, so a sale of the farm does not automatically include quota.

faq.q: What is the ALR and does it apply to farms in Langley Horse Properties Equestrian Mls Listings?
faq.a: The Agricultural Land Reserve is farmland protected by the provincial Agricultural Land Commission. Farm use is generally allowed on ALR land, but subdividing, adding homes or using the land for non-farm purposes usually needs approval, so check a property's ALR status before you offer.
